title: Weight Gain Diet Plan: Healthy Meal Plan To Gain Weight Safely
summary: Have you ever watched a movie and thought of the question, What do actors morph their bodies into shapes for roles? Looking momentarily like a regular guy, they
body_text: Have you ever watched a movie and thought of the question, What do actors morph their bodies into shapes for roles? Looking momentarily like a regular guy, they are suddenly super ripped with bulging abs and well-defined muscles. It’s too easy to deduce that there is some secret shortcut—a magical diet or insane workout regimen known exclusively to Hollywood trainers. But these transformations result from science, discipline, and the right nutrition. Jump to section Key Principles Of A Weight Gain Diet Healthy Weight Gain Diet Plan Additional Tips For Gaining Weight Safely Wrapping It Up Look at Zac Efron. Preparing for his role in Baywatch, he didn’t just go to the gym; he followed an exact plan that included smart training and consistent clean eating. As he put it: “Your body will change if you give it the right fuel. It’s about consistency, clean eating, and training smart.” -Zac Efron. Let's be realistic—gaining muscle the right way is definitely more nuanced than the vague instruction of “eating more.” It’s easy to dive into junk food thinking that more calories easily means more muscles, which is incredibly misleading. Without the right factors, this approach leads to unwanted fat gain instead of a chiselled, lean physique. What is the most important secret? It is a smart, strategised diet containing food that builds muscle, increases energy, and supports well-being. Most people struggle with gaining weight or muscle in ways that promote health and strength, and if that’s you, know that you are not alone. The good news is it can be done with the right mindset and a few key principles to smart and healthy weight gain. Let’s explore! Key Principles Of A Weight Gain Diet Controlling and healthily gaining weight involves much more than eating more food. The aim is to increase muscle mass and strength while still remaining healthy. This entails obtaining calories from whole foods and NOT highly processed foods, having the correct balance of macronutrients, and showing consistency in your dietary habits. Gaining weight has mostly been associated with overeating or consuming highly processed foods that are low in nutritional value. Following a strategic approach ensures you gain muscle mass rather than body fat. Let’s discuss the fundamental principles that constitute a successful weight-gain diet. Surplus Caloric Intake: Gaining Weight Made Easy As it is with anything else, to gain weight, you need to eat over what your body burns, and that's referred to as surplus caloric intake or, simply put, a surplus. Achieving a caloric surplus is relatively easier, but getting it to come from nutrient-dense foods instead of empty nuggets of processed junk is where the challenge lies. Increase your caloric intake, but do it gradually in order for your body to adapt to the additions to your diet while avoiding unnecessary fat gain. Forcing excessive surpluses into your body can result in bloating and unhealthy fat gain. Helpful tip: Work towards a goal of maintaining a 300–500 calorie surplus and make sure to monitor your progress. Adjust the numbers if preferred, but only if tangible results do not appear. DID YOU KNOW? Olympic medalist Michael Phelps was said to have a caloric intake of 12,000 calories a day while training in order to maintain his energy levels and muscle mass! Balanced Macronutrients: The Right Fuel For Your Body In order to achieve a healthy weight gain, your diet should consist of the proper balance of macronutrients: Protein (30%): Important for the development and repair of muscles. Sources: Eggs, chicken, fish, lentils, dairy, nuts, and soy products. Carbohydrates (40%): The main source of muscle fuel for the body, and are necessary for recovery. Sources: Whole grain products, sweet potatoes, rice, quinoa, oats, fruits. Healthy Fats (30%): These help increase overall calorie consumption and are good for the brain and heart. Sources: Avocado, nuts, olive oil, fatty fish, coconut and seeds. These macronutrient ratios, when adhered to, will allow you to gain muscle while minimising fat storage. Tip: Consider prepping meals for the week ahead in order to ensure consistency in nutrient intake and support better balance in proportion sizes. Balanced diets prevent excess fat gain and promote lean muscle growth. YOU MIGHT FIND THIS INTERESTING: Dwayne Johnson, ‘The Rock, ' mentions eating 36 ounces of cod in conjunction with his seven meals a day for his movies. Consistency: The Secret To Success Healthy weight gain never occurs overnight, and the golden rule is consistency. Regular meals and snacks filled with dense foods will help you achieve results. Your body requires fuel to gain weight effectively. Irregular eating and meal skipping restrict your progress. Aim for 5-6 meals a day and incorporate some snacks. This constant fueling is crucial. DID YOU KNOW? In preparation for his role as Wolverine, Hugh Jackman ate every two hours, totalling 4,000-5,000 calories a day! Healthy Weight Gain Diet Plan Gaining weight does not equal eating anything and everything. It means to select certain foods that are beneficial. A meal plan needs to be designed in a way that has enough calories, protein, fats, and other nutrients available for building muscle and providing the energy required. The plan given below is simple and easy to prepare. Breakfast: A Good Start Breakfast need not be elaborated on. A great breakfast works like magic and gives the body the energy necessary for moving, performing tasks, setting the metabolism on active mode and much more. Protein Oatmeal Ingredients : Rolled oats, milk/almond milk, protein powder, banana, almond butter. Why It Works: Oats serve as a basis for nutritious complex carbs, which give energy for a long time, and protein powder serves healthy protein, while almond butter helps to give healthy fats. How to Prepare: Cook oats in milk. Combine with other ingredients: protein powder, bananas, and almond butter. Avocado Toast With Eggs On Whole Grain Bread Ingredients: Whole grain toast, Avocado, two eggs, Olive oil, salt and pepper. Why it Works: Studies do show that eggs contain high-quality protein, which helps repair and grow muscles. An avocado offers healthy monounsaturated fats, whereas toast made from whole grain provides carbohydrates for long-lasting energy. How to Prepare: Toast the bread, spread the avocado, and top with your preferred style of cooked eggs—scrambled, boiled, or poached. Season and drizzle olive oil. Do you tend to feel hungry after breakfast? Consuming more protein may help reduce your appetite and make you feel full! Morning Snack: Keep The Energy Flowing Mid-morning snacks consolidate energy levels while diminishing the chances of unhealthy cravings. Look for snacks that are dense in protein and include fibre and good fats. Greek Yoghurt Parfait Ingredients: Greek yoghurt, mixed berries, granola, honey, chia seeds. Why it Works: Greek yoghurt is rich in protein. In addition, berries and granola contribute fibre, vitamins, and minerals, while honey adds a dash of calories. How to Prepare: In a bowl, add Greek yoghurt as a base, then layer with berries and granola. Sprinkle with chia seeds and sweeten with honey. Peanut Butter Smoothie Ingredients: Peanut butter, banana, spinach, milk or almond milk, protein powder. Why It Works: Peanut butter contains a lot of calories, along with protein and healthy fats. Its flavour-free addition, spinach, further boosts the nutrient profile. How to Prepare: Blend the mixture until fully combined, and enjoy a nutrient-rich, creamy smoothie. Lunch: Power-packed Meals A nutritious lunch requires a balance of protein, complex carbohydrates, and healthy fats to maintain energy while promoting healthy weight gain. Chicken And Quinoa Bowl Ingredients: Grilled chicken breast, quinoa, mixed vegetables, and olive oil. Why It Works: Chicken provides a source of lean protein to support muscle growth, while quinoa contributes fibre and complex carbohydrates, and olive oil provides heart-healthy fats. How to Prepare: Cook chicken and quinoa, then mix them with grilled chicken and assorted vegetables. Top it off with a drizzle of olive oil. Turkey Sandwich On Whole Grain Bread Ingredients: Sliced turkey, avocado, leafy greens, mayonnaise or hummus, and whole-grain bread. Why It Works: Avocado increases the calories and healthy fats, while turkey provides a source of lean protein. How to Prepare: Make the sandwich by placing turkey, avocado, and greens on whole-grain bread. Afternoon Snack: Stay Energised Having a snack in the afternoon combats tiredness while preventing a dip in metabolism. 1. Trail Mix Ingredients: Nuts, dried fruits, dark chocolate chips, and seeds. Why It Works: It contains healthy fats and protein, making it a snack rich in calories and nutrients. How to Prepare: Combine nuts, dried fruits, seeds, and dark chocolate to enjoy this delightful mix. 2. Cheese & Whole Grain Crackers Ingredients: Cheese (cheddar, mozzarella), whole grain crackers. Why It Works: Cheese contains a significant amount of protein as well as calcium. Crackers offer some fibre. Salmon With Sweet Potato Ingredients: Grilled salmon, roasted sweet potato, sautéed spinach or broccoli, olive oil. Why It Works: Salmon is another rich source of omega-3s, and sweet potatoes add fibre and good carbohydrates. 2. Beef Stir-Fry With Brown Rice Ingredients: Lean beef, mixed vegetables, brown rice, soy sauce, sesame oil. Why It Works: Beef provides considerable protein, while brown rice is a source of energy for longer periods. Let’s talk about some of the targeted actions you can take to help you gain weight in a safe and efficient manner. Prioritise Foods High In Nutrients Considering you want to increase your caloric intake, it is just as important to focus on nutrient-dense foods that will make the weight gain healthy and support muscle growth. Instead of getting fast food that is high in calories, focus on unprocessed foods like dairy products, avocados, or whole-grain bread. This will not only help increase your weight but also improve your health. Maintain An Active Lifestyle With Strength Training Simply eating more will not lead to healthy weight gain. It should be accompanied by strength training. Regular resistance exercises help remove fat and add lean muscle to your body instead. These aid in ensuring that your weight gain increases your body's endurance and strength. Aim for 3 to 4 days a week of strength training if your goal is muscle growth. Focus on compound exercises, which include squats, deadlifts, bench presses, and pull-ups. Tip: Only a healthy mind can sustain a healthy body; this goes vice versa. So, we shall give you a crucial tip for practising yoga in your daily routine. The best for calming and relaxing your mind. For professional guidance, do contact Nirva Health for online sessions. Eating More Frequently If you struggle with large meals, try portioning them and eating more frequently throughout the day. Having 5 to 6 well-balanced meals on a daily basis will ensure that your body is getting a steady dose of calories alongside nutrients, which promotes steady weight gain. Avoid Skipping Meals By skipping meals, you risk slowing your metabolism, and it will become increasingly harder to lose weight. As a negative effect of skipping meals, you become deficient in nutrients, which leaves you feeling weak and sluggish. Try to develop the habit of having three main meals and two snacks at consistent times throughout the day, alongside two snacks to maintain calorie intake. Wrapping It Up Achieving healthy weight gain involves strategically nourishing your body rather than incorporating excessive empty calories. Like any goal worth accomplishing, it takes time and dedication to achieve. If Hollywood actors and star athletes can achieve their fitspo fantasies with hard work and disciplined eating, then so can you with smart planning for your healthy weight gain goals. Remember, progress happens at its own pace. Stay engaged with a workout plan, eat intentionally, and focus on the little things that stack up over time. No matter if it’s muscle growth, energy increases, or just improving health in general, every action brings you one step closer to your goals. title: Commercial Insurance for Rental Properties: Landlord Guide
summary: Learn about commercial insurance for rental property, covering essential protections for landlords to safeguard their investments and manage risks effectively.
body_text: Your lease agreement outlines many of your landlord’s duties, from fixing a leaky faucet to maintaining common areas. Behind those duties is a much larger responsibility: protecting the entire property as a financial investment. To do this, landlords rely on a specialized policy designed for income-generating properties. This policy, known as commercial insurance for a rental property, covers everything from damage to the building’s structure to liability if someone gets hurt in the lobby. Knowing what this policy covers—and more importantly, what it doesn’t—is key to understanding why your own renters insurance is not just a good idea, but essential. Key Takeaways Their Policy Covers the Building, Yours Covers Your Stuff : A landlord's commercial insurance is for the structure and their liability. It won't cover your personal belongings if there's a fire or theft, which is the primary reason you need your own renters insurance policy. Comprehensive Landlord Insurance Means Faster Fixes : When a landlord has solid coverage for things like equipment breakdowns or lost rent, they have the funds to handle major repairs quickly. This means you won't be stuck waiting for essential fixes to your home after an emergency. A Well-Insured Landlord Is a Responsible Landlord : Understanding that your landlord has the right insurance shows they are serious about maintaining the property. Their diligence in reviewing and updating their policy is a good sign that they are prepared to handle problems professionally. What Is Commercial Insurance for a Rental Property? Think of commercial insurance for your rental property as a financial safety net for your business. Because yes, being a landlord means you’re running a business, and this insurance is specifically designed to protect properties that generate income. It shields you from the kinds of unexpected losses that could otherwise be financially devastating. It’s fundamentally different from your standard homeowner's policy because it accounts for the unique risks that come with having tenants and operating a rental. Essentially, this coverage protects your physical property and your liability as a landlord. If a fire damages your building or a tenant gets injured on the premises, the right policy helps cover the costs, from repairs to legal fees. It’s a fundamental part of responsible property management that ensures you can handle setbacks without risking your investment. Without it, you're personally on the hook for every mishap, big or small. Understanding the key components of this insurance is the first step toward making sure you, your property, and your tenants are properly protected, creating a more secure environment for everyone involved. Why Landlords Need It As a landlord, you face risks that go beyond what a typical homeowner encounters. That’s why specialized insurance isn’t just a good idea—it’s essential. Without it, a single incident could jeopardize your entire investment. Imagine a major storm damages the roof or a pipe bursts, causing extensive water damage. Commercial property insurance helps cover those repair costs. Or, consider a situation where a visitor trips on a loose step and decides to sue. General liability coverage is what stands between you and potentially massive legal bills. This insurance also protects your income stream. If a covered event, like a fire, makes your property uninhabitable, business interruption coverage can help replace the lost rental income while you rebuild. This allows you to continue meeting your own financial obligations, like mortgage payments, even when you aren't collecting rent. It’s about creating a resilient business that can withstand the unexpected. What This Insurance Typically Covers While policies can vary, most commercial insurance plans for rental properties bundle a few core coverages. First is Commercial Property Insurance , which covers damage to the physical structure of your building and any property you own on-site, like appliances or maintenance equipment. Next is General Liability Insurance , which protects you if you’re found legally responsible for injuries to a tenant or visitor, or for damage to their personal property. Two other common coverages are incredibly valuable for landlords. Business Interruption Insurance helps you recover lost rental income if your property can't be occupied due to a covered loss. There's also Equipment Breakdown Insurance , which can be a lifesaver. It covers the cost to repair or replace essential systems like your HVAC, boiler, or electrical panels if they fail unexpectedly due to a mechanical or electrical issue, which standard property policies often exclude. Commercial vs. Personal Property Insurance It’s crucial to understand that your standard homeowner's insurance policy will not cover a rental property. Once you begin renting out a home you own, insurers view it as a business operation, which requires a different kind of coverage. Relying on a homeowner's policy for a rental is a common but costly mistake. If you need to file a claim for damage or a liability issue, it will almost certainly be denied, leaving you to pay for everything yourself. You need a specialized policy, often called landlord insurance or rental property insurance, which is a type of commercial policy. This insurance is tailored to the specific risks of renting, from tenant-caused damage to loss of rental income. Making sure you have the right type of policy isn't just about following the rules; it's about ensuring your financial protection is actually there when you need it most. Key Types of Coverage for Landlords When a landlord insures a rental property, they aren’t buying a single, one-size-fits-all policy. Instead, they typically get a policy that bundles several types of coverage together. Understanding these key components can help you see what your landlord is responsible for and why having your own renters insurance is so important. Each piece of their policy puzzle protects a different aspect of their investment, from the physical building to the income it generates. Property Insurance This is the core of any landlord's policy. Commercial property insurance covers the physical structure of your rental building. If there’s a fire, a major storm damages the roof, or the property is vandalized, this is the coverage that pays for repairs. It protects the building itself—the walls, roof, floors, and fixtures. However, it’s important to remember this policy only covers the landlord’s property. It does absolutely nothing to protect your personal belongings, which is one of the main reasons you need your own renters insurance policy. General Liability Insurance Accidents happen, and this is the coverage that protects a landlord when they do. General liability insurance comes into play if someone is injured on the property due to the landlord's negligence. For example, if a visitor trips on a broken step that the landlord failed to fix, this insurance would cover the associated legal and medical costs. It’s a crucial safety net that handles claims of bodily injury or property damage that occur in common areas like hallways, lobbies, or parking lots, ensuring that an accident doesn't turn into a financial disaster for the property owner. Business Interruption Insurance If a covered event like a fire or major flood makes the rental property uninhabitable, a landlord can’t collect rent. However, they still have to pay the mortgage, taxes, and other expenses. Business interruption insurance is designed to cover this lost income while the property is being repaired. This coverage ensures the landlord has a steady cash flow to meet their financial obligations and, just as importantly, to fund the necessary repairs to get your home back in livable condition as quickly as possible. Loss of Income Coverage Similar to business interruption, loss of income coverage specifically protects the landlord’s rental income stream. If your unit becomes unlivable due to a covered peril and you have to move out temporarily, the landlord loses the rent they would have collected from you. This insurance reimburses them for that lost revenue, typically for a set period like 12 months. It’s another layer of financial security that helps landlords manage their business effectively, even when faced with unexpected vacancies during a major restoration project. Equipment Breakdown Insurance The essential systems in your apartment—like the heating, air conditioning, and electrical systems—are expensive to repair or replace. Equipment breakdown insurance covers the cost of fixing or replacing these critical systems if they suddenly fail. This is different from standard property insurance, which might not cover a furnace that just stops working. For you as a renter, this coverage is great news because it means your landlord has a clear financial path to fixing the things that keep your home comfortable and functional without having to pay huge sums out of pocket. Assess Your Insurance Needs and Costs Getting the right insurance is a balancing act. You want enough coverage to protect your investment without paying for things you don’t need. Taking the time to accurately assess your property, risks, and lease requirements will help you find that sweet spot, ensuring you’re prepared for the unexpected while keeping your costs manageable. Evaluate Your Property's Value and Location A great first step is to get a clear picture of your property's total value. It can be tempting to choose lower coverage limits to save on premiums, but underinsuring is a common pitfall that can be financially devastating if you need to file a major claim. Make sure your coverage reflects the true cost to rebuild, not just the market value. Your property’s location also plays a huge role. An apartment building in an area prone to hurricanes or wildfires will have different insurance needs than one in a low-risk zone. Consider regional risks when evaluating what kind of protection you need. Identify Potential Risks Every rental property comes with its own set of risks. Think through the most likely scenarios you could face as a landlord. What would happen if a fire damaged the building, leaving it uninhabitable for months? What if a tenant or visitor slipped on a wet floor and decided to sue? Landlords typically need a mix of coverages, including commercial property insurance for building damage and general liability for injuries. Thinking about these potential issues helps you understand why a comprehensive commercial insurance for rental property policy is so important for protecting your assets and your income stream. Review Your Lease Agreements Your lease is more than just a rental contract; it’s a key document that outlines financial responsibilities. Review your agreements carefully to see what they say about insurance. Many leases require tenants to carry their own renters insurance and may even specify how costs for building damage are shared. Some landlords also require tenants to list them as an "additional insured" on their policy. This provides you with an extra layer of liability protection. Understanding these clauses ensures you and your tenants are on the same page and that you’re not accidentally exposed to unnecessary risk. What Affects Your Insurance Costs? Several factors determine your final insurance premium. The biggest ones include your property's value, the size of your business, and your location. Insuring a multi-unit complex will naturally cost more than insuring a single-family home. The type of business tenants you have can also influence your rate; for example, a restaurant might be considered higher risk than a quiet office. Finally, properties in areas with higher crime rates or a history of severe weather events will generally have higher business renters insurance costs due to the increased likelihood of claims. Consider Extra Coverage Options Once you have a handle on your basic needs, look into ways you can bundle coverage for better value. Many insurers offer a Business Owner's Policy (BOP), which conveniently packages general liability and property insurance into a single, often more affordable, policy. This is a popular choice for landlords because it simplifies management and can lead to significant savings compared to buying each policy separately. Ask your insurance provider if a BOP is a good fit for your rental business, as it’s an efficient way to get comprehensive protection without breaking the bank. Choose the Right Commercial Insurance Policy Once you understand the types of coverage you need, it’s time to find the right policy. This step is about more than just finding the lowest price; it’s about securing a financial safety net that truly protects your investment. The right policy will give you peace of mind, knowing you’re covered if something goes wrong. It requires a bit of homework, like comparing your options and talking to professionals, but the effort pays off. Think of it as building a solid foundation for your rental business. A cheap, ill-fitting policy can leave you with serious gaps in coverage, which is a risk you don’t want to take. Let’s walk through how to choose a policy that fits your property and your budget without cutting corners on protection. Compare Policies and Providers The first rule of shopping for insurance is to compare your options. Don't just get one quote and call it a day. Reach out to several different insurance companies to see what they offer. You’ll find that coverage details and premiums can vary quite a bit from one provider to another. While it’s tempting to go with the cheapest plan, this can be a costly mistake. Many landlords underinsure their properties to save a few dollars on premiums, leaving them exposed when a major event happens. Getting multiple quotes helps you understand the market rate and find a policy that offers a good balance of comprehensive coverage and affordability. Work with an Insurance Professional Navigating the world of commercial insurance can be confusing. The policy documents are often filled with jargon that’s hard to understand. This is where an independent insurance agent or broker comes in handy. These professionals work for you, not the insurance company, and their job is to help you find the best coverage for your specific needs. They can translate the complex terms, point out potential coverage gaps you might have missed, and ensure you’re not overlooking important details. For example, they can advise you on whether you should require tenants to name you as an additional insured on their renters policy, a small step that adds a significant layer of protection. What to Look For in a Policy When you’re reviewing a policy, look beyond the monthly premium. Pay close attention to the coverage limits, which is the maximum amount the insurer will pay for a claim. Is it enough to completely rebuild your property and replace its contents? Also, check the deductible—the amount you’ll have to pay out of pocket before your insurance kicks in. A higher deductible usually means a lower premium, but make sure it’s an amount you can comfortably afford. Finally, read the exclusions section carefully. This part of the policy lists what isn’t covered. Don’t make the common mistake of getting the minimum amount of coverage just to save money; ensure your policy truly protects your asset. Avoid These Common Mistakes Being a landlord comes with a learning curve, but you can sidestep some common insurance pitfalls with a little foresight. One of the biggest errors is failing to secure adequate loss of rent coverage, which can leave you without income while your property is being repaired. Another frequent oversight is not reviewing your policy regularly. Your insurance needs can change over time, especially if you make improvements to your property or if rental laws in your area are updated. A policy that was perfect a few years ago might not be sufficient today. Set a calendar reminder to review and update your coverage annually with your insurance professional to ensure you’re always protected. A Look at Top Commercial Insurance Providers Many companies offer commercial insurance for landlords, but some have earned a reputation for their strong offerings in this area. The right provider for you will depend on your property's location, value, and specific risks. Below are a few of the top providers known for their landlord and commercial property insurance products. We recommend getting quotes from a few of them to start your comparison process. State Farm State Farm is a well-known name in insurance and offers rental property policies that can be tailored to a landlord’s needs. They provide coverage for different types of rental properties, from single-family homes to multi-unit apartment buildings, making them a flexible option for property owners with diverse portfolios. Progressive Often recognized for its competitive rates, Progressive offers customizable landlord insurance policies. They make it easy to get a quote online and adjust coverage options to fit your budget and risk tolerance, which is great for landlords who want more control over their policy details. Nationwide Nationwide provides comprehensive commercial insurance solutions that can be adapted for landlords. Their policies are designed to protect your rental property, cover liability risks, and provide loss of income coverage, offering a well-rounded package for property investors. The Hartford With a strong focus on business insurance, The Hartford offers specialized coverage designed specifically for the risks landlords face. They provide protection against property damage and liability claims, with options that cater to owners of both residential and commercial rental properties. Travelers Travelers is another major player in the commercial insurance space with robust offerings for property owners. They are known for their risk management resources and reliable claim service, providing landlords with both a solid policy and supportive services. Optimize Your Insurance Coverage Once you have a policy, the work isn’t quite done. Think of your insurance as a living document that should adapt as your property and circumstances change. Simply setting it and forgetting it can leave you with serious gaps in your protection down the road. Optimizing your coverage is an ongoing process of reviewing, updating, and ensuring your policy truly fits your needs. By staying proactive, you can maintain the right level of protection and potentially find ways to save money without cutting corners. This approach ensures you're always prepared for the unexpected and that your investment remains secure. Let's walk through the key steps to keep your insurance policy in perfect shape. Review and Update Your Policy Regularly It’s a smart habit to review your insurance policy at least once a year or whenever you make significant changes to your property. Your needs can evolve, and failing to update your coverage can leave you inadequately protected. For example, the value of your property might increase due to market changes or renovations, and your old policy limits may no longer be sufficient. A regular check-in ensures your coverage aligns with your current property value and risks. Treat it like an annual financial health checkup. Sit down with your policy documents, or better yet, with your insurance agent, to go over the details. This simple step helps you catch potential issues before they become costly problems and confirms that you’re paying for the right amount of protection—no more, no less. Account for Changes to Your Property or Business One of the most common mistakes landlords make is underinsuring their property, often to save a little on premiums. This becomes especially risky when you make improvements. Did you recently finish a major renovation, build a new garage, or upgrade the appliances across all units? These changes increase your property's value, and your coverage needs to reflect that. If you don't report these upgrades to your insurer, your policy might not cover the full cost of rebuilding or repairs after a disaster. Be sure to contact your provider anytime you make a significant change. It might adjust your premium slightly, but that's a small price to pay for knowing your entire investment is properly protected. Understand What Your Policy Excludes It’s easy to assume your commercial property insurance covers every possible disaster, but every policy has exclusions. These are specific events or circumstances that your insurance will not pay for. Common exclusions often include damage from floods, earthquakes, mold, or pest infestations. It’s crucial to read your policy carefully to understand what is and isn’t covered. Not knowing your policy's limitations can leave you vulnerable to huge financial losses. If your property is in an area prone to a specific risk that's excluded, you'll likely need to purchase a separate, specialized policy for it, like flood insurance. Taking the time to understand policy exclusions is a fundamental part of securing comprehensive protection for your rental business. Stay Compliant with Local Laws Insurance isn't just about protecting your assets; it's also about meeting legal requirements. Many states and municipalities have specific laws dictating the type and amount of insurance landlords must carry. Opting for the bare-minimum coverage to save a few dollars could put you in violation of these regulations. Non-compliance can lead to fines and other legal penalties. More importantly, if an incident occurs and you lack the legally required coverage, you could face a lawsuit without a financial safety net. Make sure you’re familiar with the landlord-tenant laws in your state and city to ensure your policy meets all necessary standards. This protects you, your tenants, and your business. How to Lower Insurance Costs Without Losing Coverage Optimizing your coverage doesn’t always mean paying more. There are several smart ways to lower your insurance premiums while maintaining the protection you need. One of the most effective methods is to bundle your policies. Many providers offer discounts if you purchase your commercial property insurance along with other policies, like general liability or your personal auto insurance. You can also consider raising your deductible—the amount you pay out of pocket before insurance kicks in. A higher deductible typically leads to a lower premium. Additionally, making safety and security upgrades to your property, such as installing fire sprinklers or a monitored alarm system, can often result in discounts. Don’t hesitate to shop around for competitive rates to ensure you’re getting the best value. Related Articles Goodcover’s Guide to Renters’ Insurance for Short-Term Rentals Why is Renter's Insurance Required by some Landlords? Should You Cancel Renters Insurance During a Recession? Frequently Asked Questions Why should I even care about my landlord's insurance policy? Think of it as a good sign. A landlord with a solid commercial insurance policy is one who has the financial resources to handle major problems. If a fire or a big storm damages the building, their insurance provides the funds to make repairs quickly. This means you can get back into a safe, repaired home much faster. It shows they are running a responsible business, which is exactly what you want in a landlord. So, does my landlord's policy cover my personal belongings if there's a fire or theft? No, it absolutely does not. Your landlord's insurance is designed to protect their property—the building structure, the appliances they own, and the physical grounds. It does nothing to cover your personal items. Your furniture, laptop, clothes, and other valuables are your responsibility. This is the single most important reason to have your own renters insurance policy. If a disaster makes my apartment unlivable, does my landlord's insurance pay for my hotel? This is a common point of confusion. Your landlord's policy may include "loss of income" coverage, which pays them for the rent they can't collect while the unit is being repaired. However, it does not cover your personal living expenses. The cost of a hotel, meals, and other temporary needs is covered by the "loss of use" portion of your own renters insurance policy. If I get hurt in a common area, like by tripping on a broken step, will my landlord's insurance automatically cover my medical bills? Not automatically. The landlord's general liability insurance comes into play if the landlord is found legally responsible for the injury because of negligence—for example, if they knew about the broken step and failed to fix it. It protects the landlord from a potential lawsuit, but it isn't a blanket medical plan for tenants. Your own health insurance would be your first line of defense for medical costs. My lease requires me to have renters insurance. How does that relate to my landlord's policy? This is a standard and smart requirement. It ensures you have protection for your own belongings and liability. Sometimes, a lease will also require you to add the landlord as an "additional insured" on your policy. This doesn't cost you anything extra, but it provides them with a secondary layer of liability protection. For instance, if a guest is injured inside your apartment, your policy would be the first to respond, protecting both you and your landlord.

title: Mission-ready timing for a GNSS-denied world
summary: As GNSS disruptions become more common, industries from defense to finance are racing to build their own resilient timing systems. But many are unaware that proven, production-ready solutions already exist – and when GNSS fails, it’s the organizations who plan ahead that stay standing.
body_text: A few weeks ago, we spoke with a financial institution racing to stitch together a backup timing system. They were spooked by outages, GNSS jamming incidents were on the rise and their compliance team was on edge about meeting MiFID II and NIS2 requirements. So they were piecing together parts from different vendors, hoping the system would hold if the satellite signal ever dropped. And we understand the concern. Fortunately, the resilient timing capabilities many organisations are now trying to build already exist. You don’t need to build what already exists At Adtran Oscilloquartz, we’ve spent years developing and deploying the technologies these teams are now scrambling to assemble – from optical cesium to Satellite Time and Location (STL) and White Rabbit . Our optical cesium clocks are field-deployed today, delivering sub-100ns accuracy and more than 100 days of holdover without GNSS. Together, these technologies offer resilient, production-ready alternatives for a GNSS-denied world – and support compliance with regulations like NIS2. You don’t need to be a survivalist, stockpiling parts and hoping for the best. You don’t need to build your own. You just need to know it’s already out there – production-ready, proven and simple to deploy. The language gets in the way Most people aren’t looking for an enhanced primary reference time clock (ePRTC). They’re looking for a way to stay operational when GNSS goes down. Terms like ePRTC make perfect sense to those of us in telecom. But for teams in finance, defense or energy, they can obscure more than they clarify. That’s why we lead with outcomes, not acronyms. Think of it like a generator for time. When the grid goes down, your generator kicks in. Our holdover clocks do the same for timing – maintaining accuracy for weeks, even months, with no satellite signal. Can your timing infrastructure hold ±100ns for 14, 40, 55 or even 100+ days without satellite? Can it recover quickly? Can it detect and mitigate jamming and spoofing? That’s the conversation that matters. You don’t need to build your own. You just need a solution that works. Drop in what you need, when you need it And the good news is, you don’t have to rip everything out and start again. Our platforms are built to integrate with what’s already there – whether that’s PTP, NTP, SyncE or something else. We support everything from sovereign time scale generation to GNSS-backup-as-a-service (GBaaS), helping organizations modernize and secure their timing infrastructure without unnecessary disruption. That includes our latest optical cesium clocks – the OSA 3200 SP and OSA 3250 ePRC – engineered for long holdover, low maintenance and a 10-year lifespan. With compact form factors and a lower price point, they bring secure, high-precision timing to a wider range of sectors than ever before. This isn’t a pilot. It’s happening. Across critical infrastructure, organizations are deploying these solutions now. In the US, our systems form part of an L3 Harris upgrade for the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA), enhancing national aviation resilience. Similar projects are underway with energy providers, financial exchanges and government networks worldwide. These aren’t trials; they’re live deployments delivering real-world resilience today. Most organizations don’t want to know how every component works. They just want to know: Will it keep us running if GNSS goes down? Will we stay compliant? Can we avoid disruption? The answer is yes. Whether you’re facing regulatory deadlines, cybersecurity risks or degraded satellite signals, we can help you drop in what you need today – and scale out over time. You don’t need to build your own. You just need a solution that works. Let’s stop reinventing secure time – and start deploying it.

title: Eyebrow Waxing vs. Threading: Why Waxing Wins Every Time
summary: If you're looking for clean, defined brows with results that last, waxing (especially at European Wax Center) might just become your new go-to beauty ritual.
body_text: When it comes to professionally shaping your brows, two methods tend to stand out above the rest: waxing and threading. Both have their fans, but if you're looking for clean, defined brows with results that last, waxing (especially at European Wax Center) might just become your new go-to beauty ritual. Let's chat about the differences and why so many of our guests swear by our signature brow wax. What is Eyebrow Threading? Eyebrow threading originates from an ancient technique that started in South Asia and the Middle East. It uses twisted cotton threads to pull hair from the follicle with precision. Threading doesn't involve heat or chemicals, which is great news if you have allergies. It can be precise when removing and shaping individual hairs, and it's usually relatively affordable. While threading can create nicely shaped brows, it does come with some downsides. Threading can be uncomfortable and may irritate your skin, especially if your skin is sensitive or it’s your first time trying threading. It also takes longer than waxing since the technician is removing hairs one by one or in small groups. Your results can vary greatly depending on how skilled your threading specialist is, and the technique can leave redness or small tears that could potentially lead to scarring. What is Eyebrow Waxing? Eyebrow waxing is a method that removes multiple hairs at once, which makes it a better option than threading or tweezing for a few reasons. First, it’s a more comfortable experience since you aren’t targeting individual hairs over and over. Second, it means waxing is a lot more time-efficient. Waxing is also great for picking up and removing peach fuzz around the brow area (difficult to do with other methods). This ultimately results in a cleaner, more defined look. At European Wax Center, all of our Wax Specialists go through in-house brow training to deliver beautiful results. They also use our signature Comfort Wax®, a strip-less wax that’s perfect for precision and shaping. Since it doesn’t need to be covered with thick strips, your waxer’s view of the brow area won’t be obstructed. After consulting with you about your preferred shape, your Wax Specialist will carefully apply wax on the desired areas, then remove it—along with those unwanted hairs. You’re left with smooth skin and defined brows that frame your face perfectly and give you a more lifted look. Key Differences Between Threading and Waxing Time Efficiency : Waxing is much faster than threading because it removes multiple hairs at once. This means less time in the waxing suite and more time showing off those gorgeous brows. Comfort : While neither method is completely painless (let's be real, we're removing hair!), waxing is significantly more comfortable since it doesn’t repeatedly target individual (or small groups of) hairs. At EWC, our exclusive Comfort Wax® takes comfort to another level, making the experience even more pleasant. It even includes beeswax to soothe, making it a suitable option for delicate skin on the face. Precision : You may have heard that threading is more precise, but professional waxing (especially with our strip-less wax) actually offers amazing control for creating that perfect arch. Our Wax Specialists are trained to create gorgeous, face-framing brows that complement your unique features. Waxing also picks up any peach fuzz around the brow, resulting in a cleaner look. Skin Benefits : Here's a bonus you might not know about—waxing gently exfoliates by removing dead skin cells along with unwanted hair. This leaves the skin around your brows smoother and more radiant. Why Waxing Wins Waxing gives you that long-lasting smoothness and precise shape that threading just can't match. By removing hair from the root, eyebrow waxing results typically last 3-4 weeks, giving you weeks to enjoy your perfectly shaped brows. It's also a time-saver and works really well for maintaining your established eyebrow shape over time. Beyond just the practical benefits, waxing offers a more complete grooming experience with professional care. Each service at European Wax Center includes an expert consultation to determine the best shape for your face and features. Why Brow Waxing at EWC Is the Preferred Choice At European Wax Center, we elevate eyebrow waxing beyond the basics. Using our exclusive Comfort Wax®, specially formulated with skin-soothing ingredients, we're able to deliver gorgeous results with less discomfort. Our highly trained Wax Specialists are experts in shaping brows to enhance your natural features, giving you a clean, polished look. The benefits of choosing European Wax Center for your eyebrow waxing needs include smooth, defined results that last 3-4 weeks, and faster service since waxing removes multiple hairs at once. Our Comfort Wax® is designed to minimize irritation and redness, even for sensitive skin. Finally, our exclusive product line is designed for waxed skin to help extend your waxing results, so your glow goes even further. Tips for a Successful Eyebrow Waxing Experience Preparation: If you use prescription retinol products like Retin-A, take a break from them about 7 days before your appointment. Clean skin is best for waxing, so try to avoid heavy lotions or oily products before you come in since these can interfere with the wax. For the best results, remove any makeup from the area before your appointment. Finally, enhance your results by exfoliating your skin 24-48 hours before your service using EWC TREAT® Face & Body Exfoliating Gel . Aftercare: After getting your brows done, give your skin a little TLC by avoiding harsh products like scrubs, retinol, or exfoliating acids around the area for 48 hours. It's also smart to skip heavy sweating and heat sources like saunas and hot tubs right after your service. Don’t forget to keep your skin healthy and happy by regularly moisturizing. Frequency: For brows that always look on point, schedule appointments every 3-4 weeks. Since facial hair can grow faster than body hair, and your eyebrows are such a visible feature, our Wax Specialists often recommend coming in closer to the 3-week mark to keep your brows looking their best. Transform Your Look With Perfect Brows When you compare eyebrow threading to waxing, the benefits of professional waxing become crystal clear. At European Wax Center, we combine premium wax with expert techniques to give you brows that enhance your natural beauty. Our approach doesn't just shape your brows perfectly—it also takes care of your skin in the process. Ready to see the difference for yourself? Transform your look with beautifully defined brows— book a professional eyebrow waxing reservation at European Wax Center today!

body_text: Paris, July 24, 2025 – The Board of Directors met on July 23, 2025, and decided, subject to decisions by the Board of Directors and the Shareholders’ Meeting which will approve the 2025 financial statements, allocation of earnings and final dividend, to amend the indicative ex-dividend dates and payment dates related to the second interim and third interim dividends and the final dividend for 2025 as follows. 2025 Type of coupon Ex-dividend dates Payment dates First interim October 1, 2025 October 3, 2025 Second interim December 31, 2025 January 5, 2026 Third interim March 31, 2026 April 2, 2026 Final June 30, 2026 July 2, 2026 In addition, the Board of Directors decided, subject to decisions by the Board of Directors and the Shareholders’ Meeting which will approve the 2026 financial statements, allocation of earnings and final dividend, the ex-dividend dates and payment dates of the interim and final dividends for 2026. 2026 Type of coupon Ex-dividend dates Payment dates First interim September 30, 2026 October 2, 2026 Second interim December 31, 2026 January 5, 2027 Third interim March 31, 2027 April 2, 2027 Final June 30, 2027 July 2, 2027 The above indicative ex-dividend dates and payment dates relate to the TotalEnergies shares listed on Euronext. ****

(2) Gross loans represent portfolio loans receivable, net of deferred fees and costs (3) Customer Deposits represents total deposits excluding brokered deposits ROCKVILLE, Md., July 28, 2025 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Capital Bancorp, Inc. (the "Company") (NASDAQ: CBNK), the holding company for Capital Bank, N.A. (the "Bank"), today reported net income of $13.1 million, or $0.78 per diluted share, for 2Q 2025, compared to net income of $13.9 million, or $0.82 per diluted share, for 1Q 2025, and $8.2 million, or $0.59 per diluted share, for 2Q 2024. Core net income(4) for 2Q 2025 of $14.2 million, or $0.85 per diluted share, compared to $14.9 million, or $0.88 per diluted share in 1Q 2025. The Company also declared a cash dividend on its common stock of $0.12 per share, a 20% increase from the prior quarterly dividend. The dividend is payable on August 27, 2025 to shareholders of record on August 11, 2025. “We are pleased with the significant progress we are making on our Strategic Plan, demonstrated by our record results for the first half of 2025,” said Ed Barry, CEO of the Company and the Bank. “Our teams continue to unlock the value of our acquisition of IFH, grow the franchise, and strengthen our diversified business model." "Although earnings did not advance quarter over quarter, our continued focus on growing commercial and industrial loans, our success at building core deposits, and our strong net interest margin have the Commercial Bank well-positioned for profitable growth,” said Steven J. Schwartz, Chairman of the Company. “As the integration of the IFH transaction progresses, we are pleased that we have been able to maintain our fee revenue above 20% of total revenue. And, in the absence of any unexpected headwinds, which do not appear to be materializing at present, our multiple growth levers provide the means to achieve robust EPS and TBV growth. This marks the 4th consecutive year that we have increased our dividend payout. Our consistent dividend payments and continued stock buybacks evidence our sustained commitment to reward our shareholders.” Reconciliation of GAAP Net Income to Core (Non-GAAP) Net Income The following table provides a reconciliation of the Company's net income under GAAP to Core net income (non-GAAP) results excluding merger-related expenses and other one-time non-recurring transactions. Second Quarter 2025 Results Earnings Summary Net income of $13.1 million, or $0.78 per diluted share, compared to net income of $13.9 million, or $0.82 per diluted share, for 1Q 2025, and $8.2 million or $0.59 per diluted share, for 2Q 2024. 2Q 2025 core net income(5) of $14.2 million, or $0.85 per diluted share, compared to 1Q 2025 of $14.9 million, or $0.88 per diluted share. Net interest income of $47.6 million increased $1.6 million, or 3.5% (not annualized), compared to 1Q 2025, and increased $10.6 million, or 28.6%, year-over-year. Interest income of $64.6 million increased $1.8 million, or 2.9% (not annualized), over 1Q 2025, and increased $14.0 million, or 27.6%, year-over-year. The increase quarter-over-quarter was driven by an increase from Commercial Bank loan interest income due to portfolio growth, while the increase year-over-year was primarily driven by organic growth and the acquisition of IFH. Interest income included $0.4 million from net purchase accounting accretion in 2Q 2025, flat compared to 1Q 2025. There was no impact related to purchase accounting during 2Q 2024. Interest expense of $16.9 million increased $0.2 million, or 1.4% (not annualized) compared to 1Q 2025, and increased $3.4 million, or 24.9%, year-over-year. The increase quarter-over-quarter was mainly due to a lower benefit from net purchase accounting accretion, as higher deposit volumes were offset by lower deposit rates. The increase year-over-year was driven by organic growth and the acquisition of IFH. Interest expense included a $0.9 million benefit from net purchase accounting accretion in 2Q 2025 compared to a $1.1 million benefit in 1Q 2025. There was no impact related to purchase accounting during 2Q 2024. The 2Q 2025 provision for credit losses was $4.1 million, an increase of $1.8 million from 1Q 2025. The increase over the prior quarter was primarily driven by $1.1 million from OpenSky™ due to higher volumes in both the secured and unsecured portfolio, and $0.7 million from the Commercial Bank due to higher charge-offs not previously provided for. Net charge-offs totaled $5.1 million, or 0.75% of portfolio loans (annualized), including $3.0 million from the Commercial Bank and $2.1 million from OpenSky™ loans. The Commercial Bank charge-offs were driven by $2.1 million from balances charged off from the acquired IFH portfolio, including a loan sale resulting in a charge-off of $1.5 million. Net charge-offs for 1Q 2025 totaled $2.4 million, or 0.38% of portfolio loans (annualized), mainly driven by $2.3 million from OpenSky™ loans. The average rate on the low-and-no interest-bearing deposits was 0.14% for 2Q 2025, a decrease of 1 bps from 1Q 2025 and an increase of 8 bps year-over-year. The investment securities portfolio continues to be classified as available-for-sale and had a fair market value of $228.9 million, or 6.8% of total assets, an effective duration of 2.7 years, with U.S. Treasury Securities representing 60% of the overall investment portfolio at June 30, 2025. The accumulated other comprehensive income (loss) on the investment securities portfolio improved $1.1 million during the quarter to negative $8.1 million after-tax as of June 30, 2025, which represents 2.1% of total stockholders' equity. The Company does not have a held-to-maturity investment securities portfolio. Liquidity – The Company maintains stable and reliable sources of available borrowings, generally consistent with prior quarter. Sources of available borrowings at June 30, 2025 totaled $834.8 million, compared to $820.9 from 1Q 2025. During 2Q 2025, available collateralized lines of credit totaled $750.6 million, unsecured lines of credit with other banks totaled $76.0 million and unpledged investment securities available as collateral for potential additional borrowings of $8.2 million. Capital Positions – As of June 30, 2025, the Company reported a Common Equity Tier-1 capital ratio of 13.58%, compared to 13.24% at March 31, 2025. At June 30, 2025, the Company and the Bank maintained regulatory capital ratios that exceed all capital adequacy requirements. Shares repurchased and retired during the three months ended June 30, 2025, as part of the Company's stock repurchase program, totaled 93,170 shares at an average price of $26.66, for a total cost of $2.5 million including commissions.
