title: What great PMs do that AI never will
summary: AI can speed up the work, but it still can’t lead. This article breaks down what great product managers do that no language model can replace.
body_text: AI can summarize interviews, generate draft roadmaps, and even write release notes. But it still can’t ask the right questions, align a team, or drive a product forward. As AI becomes more capable, many product managers are asking themselves: what’s my role now? The answer isn’t that your work is less valuable. It’s that your value is becoming clearer. The most powerful parts of product work still require context, discernment, and leadership — things no language model can replace. The strongest product managers are already adapting. They’re using AI to accelerate execution, while leaning even harder into what truly sets them apart: judgment, narrative, and momentum. Here are five ways they’re doing that — and how the right tools can help you amplify each one. 1. Choosing the right problem to solve AI can cluster data or group interview themes, but it doesn’t understand strategic timing, organizational constraints, or what actually matters to your users. It can point to a symptom, but not always the root cause. Strong PMs go further. They know how to sift through input, ask second-order questions, and align the team on what problem is truly worth solving. Sometimes, that means postponing a highly requested feature because it doesn’t solve the right thing. Other times, it means spotting a subtle but mission-critical friction pattern others missed. Tools like Dovetail and Productboard can help surface trends and structure insights, while Amplitude or Mixpanel provide behavioral data that complements your qualitative work. But it’s still on you to connect the dots and choose what to prioritize next. 2. Crafting the story that creates alignment AI can write, but not in a way that makes people care. It can’t change minds or bring people along. Strong PMs use storytelling to bring people together. They frame decisions with context, connect the work to a real user need, and show why it matters now. This kind of narrative helps teams move in the same direction with clarity and energy. Storytelling also builds product affinity. When people understand the purpose behind the work — not just the output — they care more about getting it right. You can use tools like ChatPRD to frame decisions in a structured way or Grain to capture customer verbatims that lend weight to your point. FigJam can help you map journeys visually and connect teams around shared outcomes. 3. Moving forward in ambiguity AI doesn’t know what to do when the path doesn’t exist. It can suggest options, but it can’t navigate uncertainty — and it definitely doesn’t do stakeholder management. This is where PMs lead. You move work forward without perfect data. You know when to ask for signal, when to test, and when to decide. You help teams stay grounded even when priorities shift or tradeoffs are murky. This kind of decision-shaping can be supported by tools like Miro for mapping uncertainty and assumptions, Loom for sharing context asynchronously, and Linear for maintaining focus and structure when things feel chaotic. 4. Taking ownership of the hard calls AI doesn’t take responsibility. It doesn’t feel the consequences of a missed opportunity or learn from a failed bet. But you do. The best PMs know that making the call is part of the job — even when it’s uncomfortable. That might mean sunsetting a feature early, rolling back a half-shipped experiment, or simply saying “not now” to a tempting request. You weigh tradeoffs, consider input, and move forward with conviction. Use tools like Cycle to synthesize customer input and make roadmap tradeoffs more visible. Fullstory can help you identify friction in real usage, and Retrotool allows your team to reflect on the outcomes and codify learning for next time. 5. Shaping a strong product culture AI doesn’t build trust, model behavior, or celebrate wins. But you do — and this might be the most underrated part of the PM craft. Strong PMs foster product cultures that last. You introduce rituals that help teams stay connected to purpose. You encourage curiosity, share customer love, and create space for insight to emerge organically. A simple #product-feedback Slack channel can become a source of pride and alignment. A consistent feedback loop can turn passive observers into engaged contributors. To reinforce this kind of culture, tools like Spring help you track team sentiment and uncover blind spots. Slack + Donut can strengthen cross-functional connections in hybrid teams. And platforms like Supernova allow you to turn early ideas into structured artifacts that anchor team collaboration — especially when building in AI-powered or fast-moving environments. What to do next AI is a powerful assistant, but it’s not your replacement. It can suggest solutions, but not tell you which ones matter. It can summarize feedback, but not frame the problem. It can’t take a stance, tell a story, or lead a team through the messy middle. This is your advantage. So focus your energy on what AI can’t replicate: strategic judgment, product storytelling, and human leadership. The more machines evolve, the more valuable your uniquely human skillset becomes.

title: Cheapest Renters Insurance in NJ: A Guide to Affordable Coverage
summary: Find the cheapest renters insurance New Jersey offers with our guide to affordable coverage options, helping you protect your belongings without overspending.
body_text: Let’s clear up the biggest myth about renting right away: your landlord's insurance does not cover your personal belongings. If a pipe bursts or a fire breaks out, their policy protects the building, but you’re on your own to replace your laptop, furniture, and clothes. That’s where renters insurance comes in, acting as your personal financial backstop. Many people skip it, assuming it’s too expensive, but you might be surprised. It’s one of the most affordable ways to protect your assets. In this guide, we’ll walk through everything you need to know, from understanding your coverage to finding the cheapest renters insurance New Jersey providers offer, so you can be confident you’re fully protected. Key Takeaways Renters Insurance is an Essential and Affordable Safety Net : For less than the cost of a monthly subscription, you can protect thousands of dollars worth of your belongings and shield yourself from liability claims. The Best Policy Isn't Just the Cheapest : To get real value, choose a policy with Replacement Cost Value (RCV) to fully replace your items, and always check the exclusions for things like flood damage. Simple Actions Can Lower Your Premium : You have the power to reduce your rate. Ask about bundling discounts, choose a higher deductible you can comfortably afford, and get credit for safety devices like smoke detectors. What is Renters Insurance in New Jersey? If you’re renting in New Jersey, you’ve probably wondered if you really need another monthly bill. But renters insurance isn’t just another expense—it’s a crucial layer of financial protection for you and your belongings. Unlike your landlord’s insurance, which only covers the physical building, renters insurance is designed to protect what’s inside your home. It’s an affordable way to make sure a mishap like a fire, a burst pipe, or a break-in doesn’t turn into a financial disaster. Let's look at what a typical policy covers and how New Jersey's rates stack up. What It Covers and Why You Need It Think of renters insurance as a safety net for everything you own inside your apartment. Your landlord’s policy covers the building—the walls, roof, and pipes—but it does nothing to protect your personal items. If a fire or theft occurs, you’re on your own to replace your laptop, furniture, and clothes. That’s where renters insurance steps in. A standard policy typically covers your personal property and provides liability protection in case someone is accidentally injured in your home. It’s important to know that most policies don’t automatically cover damage from floods or earthquakes, so you may need separate coverage for those specific risks. How NJ Rates Compare to the National Average One of the best parts about renters insurance is how affordable it is, especially in the Garden State. On average, renters insurance in New Jersey costs about $14 per month, which is slightly less than the national average. For the price of a monthly streaming subscription, you can protect thousands of dollars worth of your belongings. Of course, your final rate will depend on how much coverage you choose. For example, a policy with $30,000 in personal property coverage might cost closer to $18 a month. When you shop around for quotes , you’ll see just how inexpensive this essential protection can be, giving you peace of mind without straining your budget. Comparing Affordable Renters Insurance Providers in NJ Shopping for renters insurance can feel a bit like speed dating. You’re trying to find “the one” that fits your budget, covers your needs, and won’t ghost you when you actually need them. Price is a huge factor, especially in a place like New Jersey, but it’s not the only thing that matters. You also want a provider with solid customer service and a claims process that doesn’t make you want to pull your hair out. To help you get started, let’s look at a few of the top contenders for affordable renters insurance in the Garden State. Goodcover While Goodcover isn't available in New Jersey just yet, it's worth knowing what sets us apart. We're building a new kind of insurance company—one that's fair, transparent, and member-focused. We use a cooperative model, which means we take a flat fee and return any leftover money from premiums back to our members through an annual dividend. Our goal is to provide modern, affordable coverage that’s easy to understand and even easier to manage. We’re expanding quickly, so we recommend checking back to see when we launch in your state and can bring fair insurance to New Jersey renters. State Farm If you’re looking for the most budget-friendly option, State Farm is a great place to start. On average, their policies are significantly cheaper than the state average, making them a top pick for renters watching their wallets. But it’s not just about the low price. According to a MarketWatch analysis , State Farm also scores well in customer satisfaction, which is a crucial combination. Getting a cheap policy is great, but knowing the company will be there for you when something goes wrong provides real peace of mind. Their balance of affordability and reliable service makes them a strong contender for many NJ renters. Allstate Allstate is a household name for a reason. They offer comprehensive coverage options and are particularly noted for creating policies that can be tailored to specific needs. For instance, they have offerings that are especially well-suited for seniors, who may have different coverage priorities. This ability to customize can be a major plus if you have unique circumstances or valuable items that need specific protection. While they might not always be the absolute cheapest option on the block, their focus on creating a policy that fits you can provide significant value and security, ensuring you’re not paying for coverage you don’t need. Progressive For those who value a quick and painless digital experience, Progressive is a fantastic choice. They make it incredibly simple to get a renters insurance quote online in just a few minutes, which is perfect if you want to compare rates without spending your whole afternoon on the phone. Progressive emphasizes affordability and protecting your belongings from the unexpected, from theft to fire. Their straightforward approach is designed to get you covered quickly and efficiently. If you’re comfortable managing your policy online and want a no-fuss process, Progressive’s platform is one of the most user-friendly out there. GEICO GEICO is another major insurance provider that many renters in New Jersey consider. Like other large insurers, they offer a wide range of coverage options and potential discounts, especially if you bundle your renters policy with an auto policy. However, their rates and offerings can vary quite a bit based on your specific location, building, and coverage needs. The best way to see what GEICO can offer you is to go directly to their website and get a personalized quote. This will give you the most accurate picture of their pricing and allow you to compare their coverage details directly against other providers. What Your NJ Renters Policy Should Cover When you're looking for renters insurance, the price is important, but what you get for that price is what really matters. A standard policy is designed to protect you and your things from unexpected events. While every policy has its own details, there are a few core types of coverage you should always look for. Understanding these will help you choose a plan that gives you real peace of mind, not just a low monthly bill. A good policy acts as a financial safety net, catching you when things go wrong so you can get back on your feet without draining your savings. Personal Property This is the part of your policy that covers your stuff. Think about everything you own: your laptop, your couch, your clothes, your bike. If your belongings are damaged or stolen due to a covered event like a fire, theft, or a burst pipe, personal property coverage helps you pay to repair or replace them. You might not think you have a lot of valuable items, but the cost to replace everything at once can be staggering. Taking a quick inventory of your possessions can give you a much clearer picture of how much coverage you actually need to be fully protected. Personal Liability Accidents happen, and personal liability coverage is your financial safety net when they do. This coverage protects you if you're found responsible for injuring someone or damaging their property. For example, if a guest trips over a rug in your apartment and needs medical attention, or if your overflowing bathtub damages the ceiling of the unit below you, liability coverage can help pay for the associated medical bills or repair costs. It even helps cover legal fees if you're sued, which can save you from a major financial headache. It’s a crucial part of any renters insurance policy . Additional Living Expenses (ALE) What would you do if a fire or major water leak made your apartment unlivable for a few weeks? That's where Additional Living Expenses (ALE) coverage comes in. Also known as "loss of use," this part of your policy helps pay for temporary housing, like a hotel or short-term rental, if you're forced to leave your home due to a covered event. It can also cover other necessary costs, like meals and laundry, that go beyond your normal budget. ALE ensures you have a safe place to stay without having to drain your savings, which is one of the most valuable and often overlooked benefits of renters insurance. Replacement Cost vs. Actual Cash Value When you make a claim for your belongings, your insurer will pay you based on one of two methods: Replacement Cost Value (RCV) or Actual Cash Value (ACV). It's vital to know the difference. ACV pays you for what your item was worth at the time it was damaged or stolen, factoring in depreciation. So, you’ll get the value of a five-year-old TV, not enough for a new one. RCV, on the other hand, pays the full cost to replace your item with a new, similar one. While a policy with RCV might cost slightly more, it provides far better protection. We always recommend choosing replacement cost coverage to ensure you're truly able to get back on your feet. What Affects Your Renters Insurance Rate? Ever wonder how insurance companies come up with your specific monthly rate? It’s not just a random number. Your premium is a calculated reflection of risk, based on a handful of key factors. Some of these are about your home and location, while others are tied to the coverage you select and even your personal financial habits. Understanding what goes into this calculation is the first step toward finding a policy that fits your budget without sacrificing the protection you need. Let’s break down the main components that shape your renters insurance rate. Your Location and Building Type It’s true in real estate and it’s true in insurance: location matters. The cost of your policy depends heavily on your specific location in New Jersey , as some areas have higher risks than others. Insurers look at neighborhood crime statistics, the frequency of weather-related claims nearby (like from coastal storms), and even how close your rental is to a fire station or fire hydrant. The type of building you live in also plays a part. A newer apartment building with modern wiring and sprinkler systems might earn you a lower rate than an older home, which could be seen as having a higher risk of fire or plumbing issues. Your Coverage Amount and Deductible You have direct control over two major levers that influence your premium: your coverage amount and your deductible. The coverage amount is the total value your policy will pay out to replace your belongings. Your deductible is the amount you agree to pay out of pocket before your insurance coverage kicks in on a claim. Choosing a higher coverage limit will increase your premium, while opting for a higher deductible can lower your monthly payments. It’s a balancing act. You want enough coverage to protect your assets, but you also want a deductible you can comfortably afford if you ever need to file a claim. The Value of Your Belongings To pick the right coverage amount, you first need a clear picture of what your stuff is worth. It’s easy to underestimate the total value of your clothes, furniture, electronics, and kitchenware. Take some time to create a home inventory—a simple list or spreadsheet of your possessions and their estimated replacement cost. This exercise does more than just prepare you for a potential claim; it ensures you have enough coverage to replace your belongings without being underinsured. Guessing on this number could leave you paying out of pocket to replace essential items after a fire or theft. Your Credit History This one might come as a surprise, but your financial background can play a role. Many insurers use a credit-based insurance score when setting your rates. This isn't the same as your FICO score, but it's derived from your credit report. The logic is that industry data shows a correlation between how a person manages their finances and their likelihood of filing a claim. While it’s just one piece of the puzzle, a stronger credit score can impact your insurance rates in a positive way, potentially leading to a lower premium. It’s another reason why maintaining good credit habits is so important. How to Get a Lower Renters Insurance Premium Renters insurance in New Jersey is already quite affordable, but who doesn't love saving a little extra cash? Getting a lower premium is often easier than you think. It just takes a few smart moves to make sure you’re getting the best deal possible without sacrificing the coverage you need. Here are a few straightforward strategies you can use to reduce your rate. Bundle Your Policies One of the most common and effective ways to save is by bundling your policies. If you have auto insurance, check with your provider to see if they also offer renters insurance. Insurers love when you buy multiple products from them and will often reward you with a multi-policy discount. This can be a significant price break on both your car and renters policies. It simplifies your life by having one company to deal with and saves you money in the process. It’s a win-win, so always ask about bundling when you’re shopping for quotes. Raise Your Deductible Your deductible is the amount of money you agree to pay out-of-pocket before your insurance coverage kicks in on a claim. Think of it as your share of the cost. Choosing a higher deductible will almost always lower your monthly premium. For example, increasing your deductible from $250 to $500 or $1,000 can lead to noticeable savings. The key is to pick a deductible amount you could comfortably pay tomorrow if something happened. Don't set it so high that you couldn't afford to cover it, as that defeats the purpose of having good insurance coverage in the first place. Install Safety and Security Devices Insurance companies are all about managing risk. The safer your apartment is, the less likely you are to file a claim—and insurers will often reward you for it. You can earn discounts by installing protective devices in your rental. This includes things like smoke detectors, fire extinguishers, deadbolt locks, and a central security or burglar alarm system. Make sure to tell your insurance provider about any safety features your apartment has. Even if your landlord installed them, you could still be eligible for a discount. It’s an easy way to get credit for being a low-risk tenant and lower your premium. Maintain a Good Claims Record Your claims history plays a big role in what you pay for insurance. If you go years without filing a claim, insurers see you as a responsible, low-risk customer. Many companies offer a "claims-free" discount to policyholders who have a clean record for a certain number of years. This is why it’s sometimes better to handle very small losses yourself instead of filing a claim. A minor claim might only get you a small payout, but it could cause your premium to increase at renewal time. Carefully consider whether filing a claim is worth potentially losing your discount and paying higher rates in the future. How to Compare Policies Beyond the Price The lowest price tag is always tempting, but when it comes to renters insurance, the cheapest option isn't always the best. A policy that doesn't provide enough coverage or comes from a company with terrible service won't do you much good when you actually need to file a claim. To find a policy that offers real value and peace of mind, you need to look past the monthly premium and examine what you’re truly getting for your money. Here’s how to evaluate your options like a pro. Check Coverage Limits and Add-Ons This is where the details really matter. A standard policy will cover your personal belongings and liability, but the amount of coverage can vary wildly. Make sure the policy covers everything you own, from your laptop and TV to your furniture and clothes. Pay close attention to sub-limits, which are caps on specific categories like jewelry or electronics. If you have a high-end computer or a valuable collection, you might need to purchase an add-on, or "endorsement," for extra protection. Taking a quick home inventory can help you figure out exactly how much coverage you need so you don't end up underinsured. Understand Deductibles and Premiums Your premium is what you pay each month, and your deductible is what you pay out-of-pocket before your insurance coverage starts. These two numbers have an inverse relationship: a higher deductible usually means a lower monthly premium, and vice-versa. While a lower premium is attractive, you need to "choose a deductible you can comfortably afford," as financial experts at MarketWatch advise. Think about it this way: if your apartment was burglarized tomorrow, could you easily come up with $1,000 for the deductible? If not, a policy with a lower deductible, like $250 or $500, might be a better fit, even if it costs a few more dollars each month. Look into Customer Service Reviews When you need to use your insurance, you’ll be dealing with a company during a stressful time. A low price won't make up for a frustrating customer service experience. Before you commit, spend some time reading what current and former customers have to say. Check online reviews to see how people describe their interactions with the company. Are they responsive and helpful, or are there complaints about long wait times and unhelpful representatives? A company’s reputation for service can tell you a lot about what you can expect if you ever need to reach out for help or to file a claim. Research the Claims Process Ultimately, you’re buying renters insurance for the promise that your provider will be there to help you recover after a loss. That’s why the claims process is so important. Some companies make it incredibly simple with streamlined mobile apps and 24/7 support, while others might have a more old-school, paper-heavy process. Look for information on the insurer's website about how their claims process works. Reading reviews that specifically mention filing a claim can give you invaluable insight. As reviewers at ValuePenguin note, some companies are known for excellent customer service, which often translates to a smoother claims experience. A hassle-free process can make all the difference when you’re trying to get back on your feet. Common Myths About Renters Insurance When it comes to renters insurance, a few common misunderstandings can leave you unprotected when you need it most. Let's clear up some of the biggest myths so you can make sure you have the right coverage for your home. Myth: Your Landlord's Policy Covers Your Stuff This is one of the most frequent and costly misconceptions. It’s easy to assume your landlord’s insurance has you covered, but their policy is designed to protect the building itself—the walls, roof, and floors. It does not cover your personal belongings. If there’s a fire, theft, or water damage, you’ll need your own renters insurance policy to replace your furniture, electronics, clothes, and other items. Think of it this way: your landlord insures their house, and you insure your home. Myth: It's Too Expensive Many people skip renters insurance because they think it’s a major monthly expense. The truth is, it’s one of the most affordable types of insurance you can buy. Most policies cost between $15 to $30 a month, which is likely less than you spend on streaming services. When you consider that it protects thousands of dollars worth of your belongings and provides liability coverage, you’ll find that renters insurance is a cost-effective way to secure your financial peace of mind. It’s a small price to pay to avoid a huge financial hit down the road. Myth: Your Roommates Are Automatically Included Living with roommates is a great way to save on rent, but don't assume you can share a renters insurance policy. A standard policy only covers you and your belongings, along with resident relatives. Your roommate is not automatically included. For everyone in the apartment to be protected, each person generally needs their own policy. Some companies allow you to add a roommate, but it can complicate things if you have to file a claim. The simplest and safest route is for each roommate to get their own coverage. Myth: You Only Need It If You Have Expensive Things You might look around your apartment and think, "I don't own anything that valuable." But the cost of replacing everything at once adds up faster than you’d expect. Think about your laptop, TV, all your clothes, kitchen appliances, furniture, and even your toothbrush. The cumulative value of your belongings is likely much higher than you realize. Renters insurance isn’t just for people with fine art or expensive jewelry; it’s for anyone who would struggle to replace all their personal items out of pocket after a disaster. Does Your Policy Cover Natural Disasters in NJ? New Jersey sees its fair share of wild weather, from coastal storms to inland flooding. While your renters insurance policy is a financial safety net for many situations, it doesn’t cover every act of nature. Understanding the specific exclusions for natural disasters is key to making sure you have the protection you actually need before a storm hits. Reading the fine print now can save you a massive headache later. Let's break down what's typically covered and what isn't. Know What Standard Policies Exclude This is the most important thing to get straight: your standard renters policy does not cover everything. The biggest exclusions are almost always flood and earthquake damage. So, if a nearby river overflows or a hurricane causes a storm surge that floods your ground-floor apartment, your basic policy won't pay to replace your ruined furniture or electronics. It’s one of the most common myths about renters insurance . Reading your policy documents carefully is the only way to know for sure what’s on the exclusion list. Don't just assume you're covered. Consider Separate Flood Insurance Because flood damage is excluded from standard policies, you need a separate policy for it. If you live anywhere near the Jersey Shore or in a low-lying area prone to flash floods, this is something you should seriously consider. You can typically get this coverage through the National Flood Insurance Program (NFIP), managed by FEMA. It's worth checking your address on FEMA’s flood maps to see your property's risk level. A little research now can help you decide if the extra policy is a worthwhile investment. Check Your Hurricane and Storm Coverage This is where things can get tricky. Your renters policy will likely cover damage from wind and hail during a hurricane. For example, if high winds shatter your window and rain soaks your laptop, you're probably covered. However, the policy will not cover damage from flooding caused by the storm surge. That’s the critical difference. You should also check if your policy has a separate, higher "hurricane deductible," which is common in coastal states. This means you'd pay more out of pocket for a hurricane claim than for a fire claim. Understanding your storm coverage before the season starts is essential. How to Choose the Right Policy for You Picking the right renters insurance policy doesn't have to be overwhelming. It’s about finding the sweet spot between what you can afford and the coverage that lets you sleep at night. Once you know what to look for, you can confidently choose a plan that protects your home and your wallet. Let's walk through the key steps to finding the perfect policy for your New Jersey apartment. Figure Out How Much Coverage You Need First, figure out what your stuff is worth by creating a home inventory. This helps you choose the right amount of personal property coverage. The amount you choose directly affects your premium. You'll also select a deductible—the amount you pay before insurance kicks in. A higher deductible can lower your monthly payment, but make sure it’s an amount you can comfortably afford if you need to file a claim. Use Online Tools to Compare Quotes Don't settle for the first insurance quote you get. Shopping around is the best way to find affordable coverage. In fact, comparing quotes from different companies can save you hundreds of dollars a year. Use online tools to get quotes quickly. At Goodcover, we make it simple to see your rate with a clear, straightforward quote in minutes so you can see how we stack up. Ask an Agent the Right Questions Price is important, but so is the quality of service. Before you commit, do a little digging. Check online reviews to see what current customers are saying about their experience, especially when it comes to filing a claim. Don't be shy about asking an agent about available discounts, how the claims process works, and what their communication is like. Getting answers upfront helps you understand what to expect from the company. Always Read the Policy Exclusions This might be the most important tip of all: read the fine print. Every policy has exclusions—specific situations or items that are not covered. A standard renters policy in New Jersey covers your belongings and liability, but it typically won't cover damage from floods or earthquakes. Knowing these exclusions ahead of time is critical. It helps you avoid unwelcome surprises and allows you to purchase separate coverage if needed. Renters Insurance and Car Theft: Everything You Need To Know | Goodcover – fair, modern, cooperative renters insurance. Does Your Renters Policy Cover Wildfire Damage? | Goodcover – fair, modern, cooperative renters insurance. Renters Insurance Facts: Debunking Common Myths | Goodcover – fair, modern, cooperative renters insurance. Frequently Asked Questions My landlord has insurance, so why do I need my own policy? This is a really common point of confusion. Your landlord's insurance only protects their property—the building's structure, the roof, and the walls. It does absolutely nothing to cover your personal belongings. If a fire or burst pipe ruins your laptop, furniture, and clothes, you would be responsible for replacing everything yourself. Renters insurance is what protects your things inside your home. I live with a roommate. Can we just share one policy? While some companies might let you add a roommate to a policy, it's almost always a better idea for each of you to have your own. A standard policy is designed to cover you and your resident relatives, not your roommate. Sharing a policy can create complicated situations if one of you needs to file a claim or decides to move out. The simplest and safest approach is for each person to get their own affordable coverage. What's the most important thing to look for in a policy besides a low price? You should always check whether the policy offers "Replacement Cost Value" (RCV) for your belongings. This means if your five-year-old couch is destroyed, the insurance will pay for a new, similar couch, not just what the old one was worth. This single detail makes a huge difference in how well you can recover after a loss. A policy with RCV provides far more financial security than a cheaper plan that only pays the depreciated value. How do I figure out how much coverage I actually need? It's easy to underestimate the value of your possessions. The best way to get an accurate number is to do a quick home inventory. Walk through your apartment and make a list of your major items—furniture, electronics, clothes, kitchenware—and estimate what it would cost to replace them today. You don't need a perfect, detailed spreadsheet. A rough total will give you a realistic idea of how much personal property coverage to buy so you aren't left underinsured. Am I covered if a hurricane or major storm floods my apartment? This is a critical question for any New Jersey renter. A standard renters insurance policy will not cover damage from flooding, whether it's from a storm surge or an overflowing river. You would need to purchase a separate flood insurance policy for that kind of protection. However, your policy will likely cover damage from wind, so if a storm breaks a window and rain ruins your things, that part of the loss would typically be covered.

title: Community Healthcare Trust Announces Results for the Three Months Ended June 30, 2025
summary: /PRNewswire/ -- Community Healthcare Trust Incorporated (NYSE: CHCT) (the "Company") today announced results for the three months ended June 30, 2025. The...
body_text: FRANKLIN, Tenn. , July 29, 2025 /PRNewswire/ -- Community Healthcare Trust Incorporated (NYSE: CHCT ) (the "Company") today announced results for the three months ended June 30, 2025. The Company reported a net loss for the three months ended June 30, 2025 of approximately $12.6 million , or $0.50 per diluted common share. Funds from operations ("FFO") and adjusted funds from operations ("AFFO") for the three months ended June 30, 2025 totaled $0.23 and $0.50 , respectively, per diluted common share. Items Impacting Our Results include: During the three months ended June 30, 2025 , the Company determined that the collectability of the remaining interest receivable balance and unreserved notes related to its geriatric behavioral hospital tenant were not reasonably assured. As such, the Company recorded a $1.7 million reserve on its interest receivable, resulting in a reduction of FFO and AFFO per diluted common share of $0.06 for the three months ended June 30, 2025 . Also, the Company recorded an $8.7 million credit loss reserve on its notes receivable with the tenant. Because the Company views its notes receivable as incidental to its business of acquiring and leasing real estate, the $8.7 million credit loss reserve is added back in calculating FFO and, therefore, does not impact FFO or AFFO per diluted common share. On July 17, 2025 , the geriatric behavioral hospital tenant signed a Letter of Intent (LOI) for the sale of its business to a behavioral healthcare provider. Among other terms and conditions of the sale, the buyer would sign new leases for the six geriatric hospitals owned by the Company. However, the Company cannot provide assurance as to the timing of when, or whether, this transaction will actually close. As previously announced, the Company's former Executive Vice President, Asset Management was terminated effective May 31, 2025 . In accordance with his employment agreement, his unvested restricted shares totaling 198,015 shares vested and his unvested restricted stock units totaling 18,275 units vested at target upon his termination. Upon termination and vesting of these shares, the Company accelerated the unamortized remaining balance of his deferred compensation at May 31, 2025 . The Company recorded severance and transition-related charges totaling approximately $5.9 million , including non-cash accelerated amortization of stock-based compensation of approximately $4.6 million , which reduced FFO per diluted common share by approximately $0.22 for the three months ended June 30, 2025 . During the first quarter of 2025, the Company acquired a behavioral specialty facility for cash consideration of approximately $9.7 million and an expected stabilized return of approximately 9.5%. Because the lease had not yet commenced and was accounted for as a sale-leaseback transaction, the Company could not recognize the acquisition as a real estate purchase during the first quarter of 2025 but rather accounted for it as a financing transaction. During the second quarter of 2025, the lease commenced, the real estate purchase was recognized, and the asset was reclassified from other assets to real estate properties on the Company's Condensed Consolidated Balance Sheet. The property is 100% leased to a tenant with a lease expiration in 2040. This first quarter 2025 acquisition was funded from proceeds from the Revolving Credit Facility. During the second quarter of 2025, the Company disposed of a building in Ohio , received net proceeds of approximately $0.6 million , and recognized a gain of approximately $0.2 million on the sale. Also, during the second quarter of 2025, the Company amended an operating lease on a property that resulted in a sales-type lease. As such, the Company reclassified the real estate to other assets on the Condensed Consolidated Balance Sheet and recognized a gain on sale of the real estate totaling approximately $1.3 million . On July 9, 2025 , the Company acquired one inpatient rehabilitation facility in Florida upon completion of construction for a purchase price of approximately $26.5 million and cash consideration of approximately $26.4 million . Upon acquisition, the property was 100.0% leased to a tenant with a lease expiration in 2040 and an expected return of approximately 9.4%. The acquisition was funded with net proceeds from the Revolving Credit Facility and cash on hand. The Company has six properties under definitive purchase agreements, to be acquired after completion and occupancy, for an aggregate expected purchase price of approximately $146.0 million . The Company's expected returns on these investments are approximately 9.1% to 9.75%. The Company anticipates closing on these properties throughout 2025, 2026 and 2027; however, the Company cannot provide assurance as to the timing of when, or whether, these transactions will actually close. During the second quarter of 2025, the Company did not issue any shares under its ATM program. On July 24, 2025 , the Company's Board of Directors declared a quarterly common stock dividend in the amount of $0.4725 per share. The dividend is payable on August 22, 2025 to stockholders of record on August 8, 2025 . About Community Healthcare Trust Incorporated Community Healthcare Trust Incorporated is a real estate investment trust that focuses on owning income-producing real estate properties associated primarily with the delivery of outpatient healthcare services in our target sub-markets throughout the United States . As of June 30, 2025 , the Company had investments of approximately $1.2 billion in 200 real estate properties (including one property with sales-type leases and one property classified as held for sale). The properties are located in 36 states, totaling approximately 4.5 million square feet in the aggregate. Additional information regarding the Company, including this quarter's operations, can be found at www.chct.reit. However, since real estate values have historically risen or fallen with market conditions, many industry investors deem presentations of operating results for real estate companies that use historical cost accounting to be insufficient by themselves. For that reason, the Company considers funds from operations ("FFO") and adjusted funds from operations ("AFFO") to be appropriate measures of operating performance of an equity real estate investment trust ("REIT"). In particular, the Company believes that AFFO is useful because it allows investors, analysts and Company management to compare the Company's operating performance to the operating performance of other real estate companies and between periods on a consistent basis without having to account for differences caused by unanticipated items and other events. The Company uses the National Association of Real Estate Investment Trusts, Inc. ("NAREIT") definition of FFO. FFO is an operating performance measure adopted by NAREIT. NAREIT defines FFO as the most commonly accepted and reported measure of a REIT's operating performance equal to net income (calculated in accordance with GAAP), excluding gains or losses from the sale of certain real estate assets, gains and losses from change in control, impairment write-downs of certain real estate assets and investments in entities when the impairment is directly attributable to decreases in the value of depreciable real estate held by the entity, plus depreciation and amortization related to real estate properties, and after adjustments for unconsolidated partnerships and joint ventures. NAREIT also provides REITs with an option to exclude gains, losses and impairments of assets that are incidental to the main business of the REIT from the calculation of FFO. In addition to FFO, the Company presents AFFO and AFFO per share. The Company defines AFFO as FFO, excluding certain expenses related to closing costs of properties acquired accounted for as business combinations and mortgages funded, excluding straight-line rent and the amortization of stock-based compensation, and including or excluding other non-cash items from time to time. title: Is Muzz Male-Dominated? From A Female’s Perspective
summary: After speaking with many women, it's clear that we want to be given princess treatment. We dream of a fairy tale ending, that ‘meet-cute’.
body_text: A few years ago, Shahzad (the CEO of Muzz) said in an article , “membership is two-thirds male and one-third female” . After using Muzz as a woman and meeting my partner on the app, we can both say that this statistic is still the same. For me, I had endless profiles to scroll through and tap the little heart icon on. For him? He said he was “lucky” if he got “one or two” that he actually “liked” . Looking for your soulmate? You won’t find your soulmate on this blog post but you might find them on Muzz - the world’s biggest Muslim dating and marriage app. Sign Up muzz Percentage of Muzz users who are female versus male. Image: Saarah Miah. So…why the imbalance? After speaking with many women, it’s clear that we want to feel like royalty and be given the good old princess treatment. We dream of that fairy tale ending. Or we simply want a ‘meet-cute’. And for some, saying we met someone online just doesn’t sound very… romantic. We want a story that will melt our mum’s heart or impress our nosey aunties. “He requested me”, “he slid into my DM’s” and “we matched on an app” doesn’t always feel like that. A lot of people who’ve met their partners on Muzz end up with creative cover stories, from “we met at Queen Mary’s. I bumped into him at the library” to “we met at some coffee shop in East London. I spilled coffee on him and he offered to get me another”, and can even go as far as “we met outside Regent’s Park Mosque, and he prayed for me”. But me? I met my partner on Muzz. And honestly? Our story is romantic. I downloaded the app and became a member because I was doing research for an investigative feature : I was sceptical about Muslim dating/marriage apps. Turns out, I didn’t need to be, because I found my match. And he said something I’ll never forget: “I wanted to take part in your investigative feature because I wanted to get to know you. I wanted to support you–personally, academically and professionally. I’d always want to support you in those ways as your partner… and I do want to be your other half.” Romantic, right? Even if it doesn’t feel romantic straight away, that doesn’t mean it won’t be more romantic later. He might take you on a thoughtful date. He might surprise you with your favourite flowers. He might even cook your favourite foods. It can turn into something romantic, and more importantly, something real. A dinner date. Image: Saarah Miah. Some even called the app “shallow”. My partner told me one of his friends “would just like profiles based purely on how a woman looked”. He wouldn’t even bother reading their taglines, bios or about me. But honestly? I wouldn’t call the app shallow, I’d say some people can be. It’s made for muslims to meet and I guess many fall victim to playing the blame game. Apps can’t stop shallow people joining and bridle how they behave. Like in real life, those are the ones you need to filter through. It’s all part of the process and helps you spot who’s serious and who’s not. Muzz also gives you tools to make that easier, too. You can filter for completed bios, shared interests, personality traits, and of course report or block anyone who’s misbehaving. I experienced this myself a lot before I had set the filters. I took my time and thought about what I wanted to write in my tagline. I wanted to show my personality, so I went for something short and sweet: “A literature graduate turned journalism student who loves animals more than people. I’m also a big fat foodie who would like to travel more.” But at the bottom of my bio, I wrote: “I’m an MA Journalism student, and I’m on Muzz because I am writing an investigative feature. I’m also genuinely looking for a partner. If you’re interested in participating and ok with your name and picture being published, message me!” How many men actually read that? We’d match, I’d ask something like, “So you’re ok with participating?” or “So you’ve read my bio?” and they’d be like “Huh, participate in what?” or they’d read my bio and unmatch. That’s when I realised most of them just liked me for what I looked like, not for who I was. And honestly? If that’s your approach, you’ll never find a match. You get what you put in. It was the ones who messaged me things like, “ So, have you got your pen and paper ready?” who had actually read my tagline, my bio, and about me. Those were the ones who I matched with. Liking a profile and matching. Image: Saarah Miah. So, while there might be more men on Muzz, I wouldn’t say it’s dominated by males. If anything, it just means we women have the upper hand. We’re spoilt for choice, and that’s not a bad thing. We decide who to match with, who to chat to, and what kind of story we want to write for ourselves. And with more women joining the app every day, that so-called imbalance? It’s starting to even out. So take your pick! Article Written by Saarah Miah, MA Journalism Student and Freelance Journalist

title: Uranium Energy Corp Announces Results of Annual General Meeting
summary: /CNW/ - Uranium Energy Corp (NYSE American: UEC) (the "Company" or "UEC") is pleased to announce that, in conjunction with the holding of the Company's recent...
body_text: NYSE American – UEC CORPUS CHRISTI, Texas , July 17, 2025 /CNW/ - Uranium Energy Corp (NYSE American: UEC) (the "Company" or "UEC") is pleased to announce that, in conjunction with the holding of the Company's recent annual general meeting of stockholders on July 17, 2025 (the "AGM"), the following proposals were duly ratified by the Company's stockholders in the following manner: Amir Adnani , Spencer Abraham , Vincent Della Volpe , David Kong , Gloria Ballesta and Trecia Canty were elected to the Board of Directors of the Company; PricewaterhouseCoopers LLP, Chartered Professional Accountants, were appointed as the Company's independent registered accounting firm; and the Company's non-binding vote on executive compensation was approved – with 95% in favor. Details of the voting will be provided by the Company in a Form 8-K Current Report filing to be made shortly. Following the AGM the following Executive Officers of the Company were re-appointed by the Board of Directors of the Company: Amir Adnani: President and Chief Executive Officer; Josephine Man: Secretary, Treasurer and Chief Financial Officer; Scott Melbye Executive Vice President; and Brent Berg Senior Vice President, U.S. Operations. About Uranium Energy Corp Uranium Energy Corp is America's largest and fastest growing supplier of uranium needed to produce safe, clean, reliable nuclear energy. UEC is advancing the next generation of low-cost, environmentally friendly ISR mining uranium projects in the United States and high-grade conventional projects in Canada . The Company has three ISR hub-and-spoke platforms in South Texas and Wyoming . These production platforms are anchored by licensed Central Processing Plants that will be served by a pipeline of satellite ISR projects, including seven that already have their major permits in place. In August 2024 , operations were restarted and ramp-up commenced at the Christensen Ranch Project in Wyoming , sending uranium loaded resin to the Irigaray Plant (Wyoming Powder River Basin hub). Additionally, the Company has diversified uranium holdings including: (1) one of the largest physical uranium portfolios of U.S. warehoused U3O8; (2) a major equity stake in Uranium Royalty Corp., the only royalty company in the sector; and (3) a Western Hemisphere pipeline of resource stage uranium projects. The Company's operations are managed by professionals with decades of hands-on experience in the key facets of uranium exploration, development and mining. title: How True Glory Hair Increased Sales and Simplified Fulfillment with Nash
summary: Learn how True Glory Hair, a Shopify merchant, uses Nash to power fast local delivery within 30 miles, boosting sales and simplifying fulfillment.
body_text: The True Glory Story ‍ "This is a loyal customer base. These are women who’ve been with us since the beginning. Now they’re working professionals. We want to make it easy for them to keep coming back." ‍ True Glory Hair is a Black-owned beauty brand that sells high-quality virgin hair extensions and wigs. title: Throughput Maximization in Action: The Palisades Tahoe Model
summary: See how Palisades Tahoe cut peak wait times by 80% using Mashgin kiosks—boosting sales and streamlining operations without adding staff.
body_text: When your peak is predictable and unavoidable, you don’t just solve for speed, you engineer it. Palisades Tahoe, a high-altitude resort with over 70% of its food and beverage (F&B) revenue earned within a three-hour lunch window , offers a compelling model for peak management through strategic capacity deployment. The Peak Problem Gets Real at Scale In retail and hospitality, research consistently shows that faster service is associated with higher revenue. Food-service studies show that diners are increasingly willing to trade wait time for service quality and cost, with many opting to abandon long lines entirely. In this context, standing still is falling behind, especially when your crowd comes all at once. Why Kiosks Scale Where Registers Stall Conventional registers require one cashier per lane. Adding lanes means hiring and scheduling cashiers, which is an inefficient and costly process. Kiosks flip that model: one or two staff can manage many machines, and each transaction happens in seconds. For Palisades Tahoe , this meant scaling through capacity, not staff: 26 kiosks across seven venues Wait times slashed from ~15 minutes to under 2 Peak-day sales climbed up to 40% That’s faster flow, higher revenue, and better staff productivity—all without expanding the kitchen or ballooning labor costs. Planning for Throughput: What Palisades Got Right Operators considering the throughput-maximization route can learn from Palisades: Size your fleet by peak load: Map guest and transaction volumes during your busiest window to determine the optimal kiosk count. Design floor flow intentionally: Arrange kiosks to channel guests through one, two, or three checkout lanes. Optimize staffing ratios: Track kiosks per staff ratio, ideally 3-4 kiosks per employee, to ensure timely technical assistance without excess headcount. Educate guests upfront: During early deployment, station guides should be positioned near kiosks to triage issues and reinforce self-service norms. Monitor throughput in real time: Dashboards to track transaction pace—adjust machine placement or staffing dynamically as needed. With this approach, the goal isn’t just peak readiness; it’s consistent throughput performance across every lunch rush. When Throughput Makes Sense and When It Doesn’t Throughput maximization is most effective in environments where operators encounter large, predictable peaks that are challenging to mitigate through other means. Resorts like Palisades Tahoe fit this profile perfectly. Most guests want to eat at roughly the same time, and few are willing to schedule their lunch hours in advance. The same holds for corporate campuses with fixed lunch windows, stadium concessions during halftime, and large student dining halls between classes. In these settings, operators can confidently plan for the surge and invest in kiosk capacity that directly matches demand. Physical space also plays a key role. Throughput maximization depends on having sufficient space to install multiple kiosks and design the customer flow accordingly. Operators with enough floor space can convert square footage into transaction capacity, eliminating the need for additional staffing by utilizing hardware that scales. But not every operation lends itself to this model. If peak volumes fluctuate unpredictably or space is limited, adding more kiosks may not be a practical solution. Some operators may also prefer greater control over kitchen pacing, especially when dealing with complex, made-to-order menus or highly variable guest schedules. In such cases, a demand-smoothing strategy centered on mobile ordering and self-service ordering tablets can provide a more precise way to manage both customer flow and kitchen workload. The Takeaway Throughput maximization is about engineering your operation around predictable demand peaks. It’s a high-speed, high-capacity strategy designed to crush the curve. Palisades Tahoe shows how combining volume, space planning, and kiosk tech can turn a challenge into a clear advantage. In the next post, we’ll explore a different path: how Cleveland Clinic uses mobile and Byte to decentralize peak management—and what that looks like in practice.

title: Introducing Branching 2.0
summary: Create, review and merge Supabase branches all within the dashboard.
body_text: Branching has been a part of Supabase for some time now, a way for you to experiment or build out new features without affecting your production environment. It requires you to connect your Supabase project to a GitHub repository which automates many parts of the workflow, but this also alienates those who prefer not to use Git. Today, we are announcing Branching 2.0 which removes the Git requirement and makes it super simple to spin up new branches. What is branching? # A Supabase branch is essentially a copy of your Supabase project, minus the data. Rather than making risky changes to your production database, edge functions or configuration, you instead spin up a preview branch and make the changes there. This gives you a safe, isolated environment to work from. When you’re happy with your changes, you merge them back into production. Current behavior # The current implementation of branching requires a connection to a GitHub repo. For every GitHub pull request created, a corresponding Supabase branch is also created and kept in sync. Database schema/migrations, functions and configuration all stored within your repo and synced up to Supabase when your commits are pushed. For those who want to work in a local and code first way, this is an ideal workflow, however, this is not suitable for those who prefer to work in a database first or no-code way, including AI Builders. New behavior # With these new updates you can now create branches with Git, without Git, or a combination of both. This can be done directly through the dashboard, Supabase CLI, or the Management API . Every branch is a direct copy of production, including schema, functions and configurations. You can then connect your app, make changes, and when ready to launch, you have the option to pull those changes down to your codebase or review and merge without leaving the dashboard. For those using separate Supabase projects for this, you no longer need to do so. How it works # For this walkthrough we’ll focus purely on a Gitless workflow. If you are someone who prefers to work in a code-first way, you can view our more extensive guide to branching . Create a new branch. # Give your branch a name, optionally sync it to a GitHub branch. If your production branch has previous migrations (e.g., via CLI db push ) then these will be run on the new branch. If your production branch has no previous migrations (e.g., all edits have been made through the Table Editor) then a db dump will be performed and run as a migration. Make changes to the new branch # Use the table editor, SQL editor, connection string or any other means to make changes to your schema or functions. Open a merge request # You, someone in your team, or the Supabase Assistant can then review the changes made via the merge page. Pull in latest updates from production # If your branch schema or edge functions are out of date, you will first need to pull in the latest changes from production. Note that by doing this any edge function modifications will be lost but new functions will remain in place untouched. Merge to production # When ready, click the merge button and watch your changes be deployed to production. If your branch is a preview branch you can now choose to remove it or keep it open. Current limitations # There are a few limitations you should be aware of before deciding to use branching without git. Custom roles created through the dashboard are not captured on branch creation. Branches can only be merged to main; merging between preview branches is not supported. If your branch is out of date, you can pull in latest changes from main, but keep in mind that all functions will be overwritten. Deleting functions must be done manually on main branch. Migration conflicts must be manually resolved on the preview branch. If you have run migrations on main, new branches will be created from existing migrations instead of a full schema dump. When to use # The following table can help you decide whether to use branching with or without git. Git Without Git Isolated environment ✅ ✅ Friction Low code No code Ease of use Extensive repo setup One click from dashboard Merging to production via Pull Request via Merge Request Conflict resolution File based None Version control Config as code Only migrations are tracked End state # We ultimately want you to be able to work in a way that produces the highest quality software in the shortest time possible. Your workflows may change as you, your team or your product evolves, and we must allow you to move between workflows seamlessly. If you want to start building directly in the dashboard then later move everything to a codebase, you should be able to do that. If you want to spin up a branch for prototyping then later pull down changes to a local migration, that should also be possible. We aren’t quite there yet, but through the combination of our CLI and web interface, that vision is closer than ever. Getting started # We want to stress that these branching updates are in their early stages and thus behind a feature preview. Anyone can opt-in to them via the dashboard but before you do, please read through the existing limitations as it might not yet be suitable for your use case. If you do make use of branching, please reach out with feedback, we’d love to hear it.

title: Colony Bank Welcomes Jordan Priddle as Tallahassee Market President
summary: Colony Bank welcomes Jordan Priddle as Tallahassee Market President, leading its banking team across the Florida panhandle.
body_text: Colony Bank is pleased to announce that Jordan Priddle has joined the Bank as Tallahassee Market President. With a strong and experienced banking team already serving this region, Priddle’s appointment reflects Colony’s commitment to continued growth and expanded capabilities in both Tallahassee and across the Florida Panhandle. The Bank has an established presence in these markets and remains focused on meeting the evolving needs of businesses and communities throughout North Florida. Priddle brings a strong background in commercial banking, most recently serving as Vice President, Corporate Banker at Capital City Bank. Over the past five years, he has held a variety of banker roles, developing a deep understanding of the financial needs of businesses throughout the area. Prior to entering the banking industry, Priddle worked as a Senior Accountant at Faulk & Winkler, LLC, and is a Certified Public Accountant. He earned his Bachelor of Science in Accounting from the University of New Orleans. “We’ve built a strong team in this market and look forward to being able to provide the businesses in this area with an even greater level of service and knowledge,” said Kyle Phelps, President of Emerging Markets at Colony Bank. “Having worked with Jordan previously, I know firsthand the value he brings to our clients and our team.” Ed Canup, Chief Banking Officer and Executive Vice President, added, “We’re pleased to welcome Jordan to Colony Bank. His leadership will be a tremendous asset to our team as we continue to grow and deliver exceptional service across the North Florida region.” In addition to his professional experience, Priddle is active in the Tallahassee community. He served on the Board of the Ronald McDonald House Charities of Tallahassee from 2021 to 2024, participated in United Way of the Big Bend’s Loaned Executive Program, and volunteers with his church’s youth ministry, serving both middle and high school students.n. title: Connect any AI Voice Agent to MCP with Retell AI MCP Node (Guide)
summary: In this tutorial, learn how to use Retell AI’s Model Context Protocol (MCP) to securely connect your voice agents to any external API or tool—like Zapier, CRMs.
body_text: Supercharge What Your Agent Can Do Securely Retell AI’s MCP (Model Context Protocol) is a powerful new feature that allows your voice agents to call external tools mid-conversation, without compromising latency, reliability, or control. MCP lets your AI agent securely interact with all your external services and tools autonomously while staying in the flow of the call. With just a few setup steps, you can securely connect to any HTTP-based service like external workflow builders like Zapier, custom APIs, cloud functions, and return structured results to be used dynamically in your call flows. In this guide, we’ll walk through exactly how Retell AI’s MCP works, what makes it powerful, and how to configure it. What Is MCP in Retell AI? MCP stands for Model Context Protocol. It allows your Retell AI agent to act as a client that securely calls a tool hosted elsewhere, like a Zapier workflow, AWS Lambda, or any HTTP endpoint, then uses the response to guide the conversation. Think of it as a secure bridge between your voice agent and the tools you already use to run your business. Why MCP Connectivity Is So Powerful for AI Voice Agents MCP is a new essential layer of infrastructure that unlocks the next level of automation. Instead of forcing developers to maintain a growing web of custom-built integrations, MCP introduces a standardized way to connect voice agents with external systems. Traditional automation systems force you to build and maintain custom integrations for each tool and use case. MCP changes that. By introducing a standardized protocol for agent-to-tool communication, it eliminates the N×M integration problem entirely, reducing the complexity of adding new capabilities as your tech stack evolves [1] . That kind of simplicity unlocks a powerful advantage: live intelligence. Instead of relying on static logic or stale training data, Retell AI agents powered by MCP can request real-time information during a call—from CRM lookups and payment checks to eligibility verification and dynamic pricing [2] . One implementation even reported reducing AI token usage by 98.8% by relying on MCP for precise external data calls instead of asking the model to guess [3] . MCP servers are proven to be faster and lighter, having shown 25% lower memory usage and 15% lower CPU utilization compared to traditional custom integration patterns [4] . That efficiency compounds at scale. While many traditional systems top out at 5–10 concurrent calls, MCP-backed voice platforms can support unlimited concurrent calls per agent, ensuring no customer is left waiting [5] . MCP adoption is driving measurable business results across industries. Early-stage users have cut development time by up to 30% and reduced maintenance costs by 25% [6] , often reaching full payback in under 90 days and unlocking long-term ROI through scalable, low-latency automation. The Core Components: ‍ MCP Server: The secure endpoint that mediates requests from your agent to your tools ‍ MCP Tool: A function on the server you want your agent to access (e.g. Send Email, Lookup Contact) ‍ Retell AI Agent: The client that initiates the request to MCP mid-call This setup lets you: Send structured requests from an agent to a tool Include headers and query params Use the result to dynamically shape the next prompt or decision Do all of this while keeping conversations fluid and real-time How to Connect MCP to Any Agent in Retell AI with MCP Node Add an MCP Server Start by going to the MCP section of your Retell AI dashboard and clicking “Add MCP” . After creating your MCP server (e.g. “ Zapier MCP ”), Add MCP Node to agent builder ‍ Paste your server URL Set timeout (default is 10,000 ms) Optionally, add custom HTTP headers like authorization tokens Set Headers (Optional) Headers let you authorize or configure your requests. For example, to pass an auth token securely: Add Query Parameters (Optional) Need to pass user inputs like age, zip code, or order number? Use query parameters with dynamic variables. Select the MCP Tool You Want to Use Once your server is added, define the specific tool or function your agent will call—like SendEmail, CheckBalance, or CreateCase. You can add multiple tools to the same server and restrict which ones your agent can access. Set Response Variables (Optional) Extract values from the MCP tool response and save them as dynamic variables for use later in the conversation.For example, you can extract a user’s name from the response and reference it later using {{user_name}}. Example response body You can save properties.user.name as a variable like user_name, and use it in follow-ups like: Why Use MCP With Retell AI? Secure by Design: Only approved agents can access specific tools Lightning Fast: Built to maintain sub-second latency Extremely Flexible: Integrate anything with an HTTP endpoint Dynamic: Capture inputs, send structured requests, and use results to personalize dialogue No Engineering Bottlenecks: Works with Zapier, n8n, or your custom stack What Can You Do With MCP? With MCP, your AI voice agent becomes even more of an intelligent operator, capable of querying live data, performing real-world actions, and adapting in real-time, all while carrying on a natural, human-like conversation. Here’s what that looks like in practice: Connect to Anything With an API MCP turns your agent into a secure, universal client that can call any HTTP-based service. That means you can instantly integrate with: ‍ CRMs like Salesforce or HubSpot to log conversations, retrieve user details, or update records mid-call. ‍ Scheduling systems like Calendly or custom booking tools to offer real-time availability and book appointments. ‍ Payment processors to check balances, verify billing status, or initiate refund workflows. ‍ ERP tools , ticketing platforms , identity verification services —anything with an accessible endpoint becomes part of the conversation. Respond With Real-Time Intelligence Instead of relying on outdated training data or static logic, MCP lets your voice agent make decisions based on real-time responses from your systems. This works across verticals: In finance , agents check application status, confirm balances, or send regulatory disclosures. In healthcare , they verify patient eligibility, surface appointment history, or trigger refill approvals. In logistics , they track packages, update delivery windows, or escalate to a live dispatcher. Automate Complex, Multi-Step Workflows With MCP, your agent can trigger full business processes behind the scenes—without the customer ever needing to leave the call. Submit a support ticket with attached metadata Start a loan application flow with validated inputs Auto-fill and send contracts or consent forms via email or SMS Initiate onboarding workflows with CRM updates, Slack pings, and follow-up emails all from a single request Because MCP supports custom headers, query params, and response parsing, you retain full control over the security, structure, and behavior of every interaction. Capture Structured Data for Analysis and Follow-Up Every MCP call can return structured data that’s saved as variables in the agent’s memory. That data can then be: Referenced later in the conversation Logged in your CRM or data warehouse Used to dynamically personalize next steps Or even passed into Retell AI’s post- call analysis workflows It’s how you turn conversations into decision-quality data without sacrificing speed or user experience. Get Started By Watching our MCP Setup Video Tutorial! Try MCP Today If you’ve been looking for a way to extend what your AI voice agent can do without bloating your workflows or degrading performance, MCP is the answer. It’s the cleanest way to keep your conversations real-time, while tapping into the full power of your backend systems. You can start building with MCP right inside the Retell AI dashboard. Start building free today! Extra Resources ‍ Retell AI MCP Docs → ‍ Retell AI MCP Server → ‍ Retell AI + Zapier Integration → FAQs Does Retell AI have MCP? Yes. Retell AI offers full support for MCP (Model Context Protocol), allowing voice agents to securely connect to any external API, tool, or system. With Retell’s MCP Node, you can configure real-time integrations that extend your agent’s capabilities—from sending emails to triggering backend workflows—without compromising call quality or latency. What kinds of tools can I connect to Retell AI with MCP? Anything with an HTTP endpoint. This includes CRMs (like Salesforce or HubSpot), scheduling tools (like Calendly), ticketing systems, databases, payment platforms, ID verification services, and no-code automation tools like Zapier or n8n. You can also connect internal services hosted on private infrastructure. How does MCP impact latency and call quality? Retell AI is optimized to maintain sub-second latency—even when calling external services through MCP. You can configure timeouts to prevent delays and ensure responsiveness. Your agent remains fluid and conversational, with zero perceptible lag in most use cases. Can I pass dynamic variables from the call to my external tools? Yes. Retell AI allows you to map dynamic variables (like customer names, form inputs, or prior responses) into query parameters or request bodies for your MCP calls. You can also include headers such as auth tokens to manage secure access. What happens with the response? Can the agent use it? Absolutely. You can extract fields from the MCP response and store them as variables. These variables can then be referenced later in the call flow to personalize dialogue, guide logic, or trigger follow-up actions. Do I need to code to use MCP? No. Retell AI supports no-code integrations with platforms like Zapier and n8n. You can build workflows visually and link them to your agent via MCP with a few clicks. Advanced users can also connect custom APIs or internal services. Is MCP secure for enterprise use? Yes. MCP connections in Retell AI are managed and scoped. You control which agents can access which tools, and you can configure headers, tokens, and authentication methods per server. MCP is trusted by enterprise teams in highly regulated environments including healthcare, finance, and telecom. Can I test MCP workflows before going live? Yes. You can test the entire flow from within the Retell AI dashboard, including request payloads, response handling, and variable logging. This ensures full confidence before deploying your agent into production. Citations [1] Daily Dose of DS. (2025). The M×N Integration Problem Solved by MCP . [2] SuperAGI. (2025).
